newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Jan-Oct vehicle sales rise 1.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Jan-Oct vehicle sales rise 1.2 pct.

text.p: Australian vehicle sales rose 1.2 percent in the first 10 months of 1996 from sales in the January to October period of 1995, the Federal Chamber of Automotive Industries (FCAI) said on Friday.
Vehicle sales for the 10 months to October totalled 540,466, up from 534,127, the industry organisation said in its monthly VFACTS publication.
Sales in October rose to 55,805 from 51,032 in September and 51,580 a year earlier.
The FCAI has forecast total Australian vehicle sales of 650,000, up 20,000 from 1995.
Passenger car sales to October totalled 409,812, up from 405,497 a year earlier, after sales of 42,486 in October, up from 39,818 in October 1995.
Truck sales for the year to date total 130,654 compared with 128,630 a year earlier after October sales of 13,319, up from 11,762 a year earlier.
Within the total truck sales, light truck sales totalled 118,198 for the year to October, up from 113,708 a year earlier, after sales of 12,013 in October, up from 10,278 in October 1995.
Heavy truck sales amounted to 12,456 for the year to October, down from 14,922 a year earlier, after sales of 1,306 in October, down from 1,484 a year earlier.
"The year-to-date 1996 market is now running ahead of the same period in 1995 by 1.2 percent or 6,339 vehicles," the FCAI said.

"The passenger vehicle market is up by 4,315 vehicles, or 1.1 percent. This is attributable to the continued strength of the small car segment, coupled with a solid performance in the upper medium car segment and to a lesser extent the luxury car segment and the people mover segment," the FCAI said.

Among the vehicle manufacturers with plants in Australia, Ford Motor Co maintained its market lead in the year to date with sales of 109,097 for a market share of 20.2 percent but this was down from a year earlier when sales of 113,593 vehicles represented a market share of 21.3 percent.
The market share of General Motors Co increased to 19.7 percent with sales of 106,715 vehicles, up from 103,515 a year earlier when its market share was 19.4 percent.
Toyota Motor Co sold 99,722 vehicles for an 18.5 percent share of the market.
In the year-earler period, Toyota sold 99,476 vehicles, which represented a market share of 18.6 percent.

Mitsubishi Motors Corp, the fourth car manufacturer in Australia, sold 49,827 vehicles in the year to October for a market share of 9.2 percent, down from 10.3 percent a year earlier when sales totalled 55,121.

The rest of the sales total was made up by imports, led by Hyundai Motor Co with sales of 42,481 vehicles making up 7.9 percent of the total. A year earlier the South Korean car maker sold 28,567 vehicles for a market share of 5.3 percent.
